 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the 2 nd respondent - insurer in O.P (Mv) No.1175 of 2015 on the file of the
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Mavelikkara, challenging the finding of contributory negligence at
the ratio of 50:50 on the part of the vehicle insured with the appellant/insurer as well as quantum of compensation awarded to the claimant.
The respondents herein are the claimant and first respondent before the tribunal.

2. According to the claimant, on 05.03.2014, at about 09.15 p.m., while the claimant was travelling in a motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-31E-1713 along Kuttitheruvu - Mavelikara PWD road, a bike bearing registration No.KL-04V- 4339 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit the claimant and he sustained serious injuries.

The claimant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation 2025:KER:73194 MACA NO. 4736 OF 2019 of 2,27,860/-, which is limited to 2,00,000/-.
3.
The first and second respondents are the rider and the insurer of the offending vehicle respectively before the tribunal.
The first respondent filed a written statement, contending that he had filed O.P.(MV) No.1015/2014 for compensation for injuries sustained, which was pending trial.
He further contended that the motorcycle is validly insured with the second respondent and that he was holding a valid driving licence at the relevant time of accident.

The second respondent - insurer filed a written statement, admitting the insurance policy but disputing the quantum of compensation claimed and the liability contending that the claimant was the tortfeasor.
Before the tribunal, Exts.A1 to A6 and Ext.B1 were marked.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 1,12,110/- and fixed negligence at the ratio of 50:50, and directed the respondent - insurer to pay 50% of the total award amount, ie, 56,055/- as 2025:KER:73194 MACA NO. 4736 OF 2019 compensation under different heads with interest @ 8%
per annum from the date of petition till realization, against the respondent being the insurer.

Challenging the finding of contributory negligence on the rider of the vehicle insured with the appellant insurer as well as the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the second respondent/ insurer has come up in appeal.
4. I have heard the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant/insurer.
Though notice was served on the respondents, they chose not to appear before this Court.

sentences.text: The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant/insurer submitted that the claimant is the accused in Crime No.559/2014 of Kayamkulam Police Station and Ext.B1 charge sheet was drawn against the claimant.
It is also stated that the first respondent, who is the rider of the offending motorcycle, preferred O.P.(MV) No.1015/2014 claiming compensation.

The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 2025:KER:73194 MACA NO. 4736 OF 2019 appellant/insurer further submitted that the accident occurred since the motorcycle driven by the claimant collided on the rear side of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-04V-4339, which was insured with the appellant herein.

Since the claimant himself was the tortfeasor, the entire negligence was on the part of the claimant himself and there was no contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle insured with the appellant and hence the insurer is not liable to pay any compensation to the claimant.

The learned Standing Counsel for the appellant/insurer also relied on the judgment in New India Insurance Co.Ltd v. Pazhaniammal & Ors [2011 (3) KHC 595], it was held that production of police charge sheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of a claim under Section 166 of the MV Act.

sentences.text: 6. I have considered the arguments raised by the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company.

2025:KER:73194 MACA NO. 4736 OF 2019 7. On a perusal of the award, it is seen that though a complaint was registered against the claimant,
he subsequently preferred a complaint before the Magistrate and the same was forwarded under Section 156(3) of the Cr.P.C, but no details are furnished regarding the fate of the afore complaint.
The insurer produced Ext.B1 charge sheet before the tribunal, wherein the police charge sheeted the claimant himself for the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle.
It is the case of the claimant that the offending vehicle came from the pocket road and hit the vehicle driven by the claimant.
Whereas Ext.B1 charge sheet would show that both vehicles were proceeding in the same direction.
The vehicle driven by the claimant hit on the rear side of the vehicle driven by the first respondent.

As per Ext.A4 AMVI report also, the damage sustained to the vehicle insured with the appellant is on the right rear side indicator, which proves that the hit was from the rear side of the vehicle ridden by the first respondent.

Though, Ext.B1 2025:KER:73194 MACA NO. 4736 OF 2019 charge sheet proved that negligence was on the part of the claimant, the tribunal found contributory negligence on the part of the claimant and the first respondent in causing the accident.

The tribunal, however,
did not provide proper or valid reasons for arriving at such a finding.

The reasons stated by the tribunal in finding contributory negligence on the part of the first respondent is as follows:
"The further aspect to be considered is whether there was any elements of contributory negligence on the part of first respondent.
The time of occurrence is 9.15 p.m.
There is nothing in evidence to show that the first respondent was riding motorcycle giving sufficient indication to the vehicles coming from the back side.
There is equal evidence to the effect that there is a contributory negligence on the part of first respondent.
In this context it is necessary to see even though another petition is filed by the first respondent, no sincere effort made by any of other respondents for simultaneous disposal of both the cases.

Hence this court is of the National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Vipin Das on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96927579/
3 view that there is contributory negligence on the part of first respondent.

sentences.text: The petitioner is only entitled to 50% of the compensation".

The afore reasons are not sufficient enough to find contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the vehicle insured with the appellant, since the charge sheet is also drawn against the claimant himself.
In this case, no other supporting evidence was adduced by the claimant to prove negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.

Moreover, though Ext.B1 charge sheet was produced by the insurer, the claimant did not care to adduce any further evidence nor mount the box to substantiate that the negligence was on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.

8. Considering the afore facts, I am of the view that since the claimant has failed to adduce any evidence to prove negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle, the tribunal went wrong in finding 50% contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed and the finding of the tribunal fixing 50% contributory negligence on the part of 2025:KER:73194 MACA NO. 4736 OF 2019 the rider of the vehicle which is insured with the appellant/second respondent in the impugned award dated 30.07.2019 in O.P.(MV)
No.1175/2015, is hereby set aside.

Sd/-
